summary: US-008 (SPIKE): Pressure-test the generalized dated-slot model
description:
**As** the team, **I want** to prove the ADR-005 slot abstraction survives the hard cases **before** US-009 (TKT-51) hardens the schema, so a bad generic design doesn't hurt every downstream vertical.

**Priority:** P0
**Type:** Spike (timeboxed, no production code — analysis + ADR amendment only)
**Depends on:** —

`risk:low` — investigation only, produces docs/an ADR, touches no service code or migration; the schema decision it produces is what US-009 implements under the full plan gate. (Challengeable: if the spike ends up needing throwaway prototype code in a service, drop the label.)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] A written analysis (in `docs/` + an ADR-005 amendment) models three stress cases against a candidate slot shape: **re-entry** (a park pass holder exits and re-enters the same operating day — multi-entry vs the single-redemption performance case), **mid-day capacity change** (an operating day's capacity is raised/cut while entries are live — where the number-of-authority lives, catalog vs inventory, and behaviour when cut below current occupancy), and **weather closure** (an operating day closes partway through — slot state, effect on already-admitted vs not-yet-arrived holders, refund signalling)
- [ ] For each case the analysis names **which attributes live on the catalog slot** vs **what the inventory claim core owns** (the ADR-005 boundary), and produces the concrete attribute set + state machine US-009 will implement (slot kind, operating hours, re-entry policy, closure)
- [ ] Verdict: the unified model holds (with the documented attribute shape) **or** a scoped exception is recorded as a new ADR — either outcome unblocks US-009 with a decided schema

Quality gate (spike): the output is a reviewed decision doc/ADR, not code; no `make check` surface. Exit is the recorded verdict.

binding.rule: Every admission-granting offer (performance, festival day, park operating day) is a dated slot in one inventory machinery; passes are entitlements to claim slot entries; lodging/day resources reserve through the same contention-safe core; slot attributes carry domain specifics — the claim primitive does not fork.

We build five Go services (catalog, inventory, commerce, payments, access) behind an API gateway, with an event bus for the domain event stream; every entity carries a tenant/organizer id from day one. Docker Compose only.

Append-only trails, one discipline: money journal is immutable/hash-chained/signed and ticket/entitlement state changes are append-only lifecycle events; trails are pseudonymous (no raw PII in any append-only record); NF525 is a later-phase profile that must layer on without schema or flow changes.

reference.summary: PRD v1 — TKT-2 catalog & event structure user stories (US-007…US-011)
ADR-005 unified dated-slot admission — the load-bearing abstraction this epic hardens; §Consequences names re-entry/mid-day-capacity/weather-closure as the pressure tests
M1 catalog baseline: 0001_catalog_schema.sql (organizers/venues/events/performances/ticket_types), publish + performance.published event, aggregated TTL reads

comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=ready kind=claim -->
Claimed TKT-50. Selection: only ticket in Ready, P0, all 7 DoR items met, no open blockers; it is the load-bearing blocker for US-009 (TKT-51) which cannot start its schema until this verdict lands.

Branch `TKT-50-slot-model-spike` created off origin/main (bfb9e27). Spike is docs-only (analysis in docs/ + ADR-005 amendment); no service code, no `make check` surface. `risk:low` upheld — investigation only, produces a reviewed decision doc, touches no migration or auth. → Planning.

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan -->
**Plan — TKT-50 dated-slot pressure-test (spike, docs-only)**

**Deliverables**
1. `docs/spikes/TKT-50-dated-slot-pressure-test.md` — the written analysis (three stress cases, each with the catalog-slot-attribute vs inventory-claim-core boundary, then the concrete attribute set + state machine US-009 implements, then the verdict).
2. Amendment section appended to `docs/adr/ADR-005-unified-dated-slot-admission.md` — records the decided slot attribute shape + state machine (the reusable decision US-009 builds).
3. `docs/adr/ADR-013-*.md` — a new ADR IFF the analysis lands a scoped exception (see verdict below); otherwise skipped and the amendment carries a plain 'model holds' verdict.

**Approach (grounded, read-only)** — anchored in the real M1 code, not assumptions:
- Re-entry: `services/access/.../0002_redeemed_lifecycle.sql` enforces single-redemption via `UNIQUE(ticket_id, event_type='redeemed')`. Multi-entry (park pass) can't fit that shape → the analysis places `re_entry_policy` (single | multi | count-limited) on the catalog slot, and multi-entry as an access-layer append-only entry/exit event stream. Separates *admission-right reservation* (inventory) from *concurrent presence* (access gate).
- Mid-day capacity: ADR-010 already decides capacity authority lives in the **inventory pool**, mutated only by an explicit new event (`cannot silently overwrite a pool that already has claims`). Analysis pins the unhandled edge — a cut below `confirmed_quantity`/occupancy — to a policy the claim core owns: block new claims, never force-release confirmed. Catalog slot carries no count.
- Weather closure: adds a `closed` slot state (catalog lifecycle, beyond draft/published/archived) + closed_at/reason, emits a domain event; inventory stops offering (archive-like but mid-live); access denies not-yet-arrived entries; refund signalling for un-redeemed holders is a downstream policy keyed off access redemption state.

**Expected verdict** (to be confirmed in the write): unified model **holds** for the reservation/claim path with the documented attributes (`kind`, operating hours, `re_entry_policy`, `closure`), capacity authority staying in inventory per ADR-010 — **but** concurrent-occupancy capping (fire-code live in/out count) is a different accounting primitive than monotonic no-oversell reservation → **scoped exception** recorded as ADR-013, explicitly out of US-009 scope (handled as an access-layer live counter).

**Test seam:** none — docs-only spike, no `make check` surface (per COS quality gate). Exit is the recorded verdict.

**risk:low upheld:** investigation only; touches `docs/` exclusively, no service code, no migration, no auth. Next: codex cross-model critique of this plan → plan-final.

<!-- sdlc:stage=plan-review kind=plan-final -->
**Plan-final — codex (gpt-5.5) cross-model critique folded in.** 11 findings, all accepted (3 BLOCKING, 7 SHOULD-FIX, 1 NIT). Each becomes explicit structure in the analysis; none rejected. Revised deliverable shape:

**Doc 1 — `docs/spikes/TKT-50-dated-slot-pressure-test.md`**, three cases hardened:
- **Re-entry (B3):** attribute is not a bare enum but `re_entry_policy {mode: single|multi|count_limited, max_entries?, requires_exit?}`; define exactly what a `redeemed` event means per mode, and how Access represents multi/count entries (append-only entry/exit stream) **without weakening the existing `UNIQUE(ticket_id,'redeemed')` guarantee for performances**. (B9) Distinguish *entitlement* (pass = right to enter) from *claim* (consumes slot capacity once) — decide whether each re-entry re-consumes day capacity (it must not for an unlimited pass).
- **Mid-day capacity (B1):** a cut below `confirmed_quantity` cannot be a bare `capacity` lower (violates ADR-010 `confirmed+held ≤ capacity`). Name the inventory representation: reject-below-confirmed vs separate requested/effective capacity vs an explicit sales-halted state — pick one, keep the pool invariant intact. (B5) Capacity source: Catalog emits the initial *resolved* capacity (today derived from venue GA); Inventory owns the mutable pool + post-publication adjustment policy (new explicit event only).
- **Weather closure (B2):** closure is **not** a new lifecycle state replacing draft|published|archived — it is `published + closure {status: open|closed, closed_at, reason}`, orthogonal to archive; define whether reopen is allowed and how it coexists with archive/public-listing. (B6) Enumerate refund-relevant Access states: entered-then-closure, exited-before-closure, no-show, re-entry-after-closure, delayed-entry-after-reopen — mark refund *policy* explicitly downstream. (B10) Closure + capacity events carry event IDs + version/sequence, replay/duplicate handling (matches existing consumed_events dedupe).
- **Added angles (B7/B8):** operating-hours must test local operating-date + timezone, opens_at/closes_at, midnight-spanning + DST — these hit the US-009 schema directly. Festival `festival_day`/shared-capacity: the slot schema must not preclude a later shared-capacity group (US-011/TKT-14 owns the claim mechanics) — captured as a non-goal constraint.

**Doc 2 — ADR-005 amendment:** the normal model + the exact US-009 attribute set + state machine (kind, operating hours, re_entry_policy, closure). **Doc 3 — ADR-013:** occupancy exception ONLY (live fire-code in/out capping = a different accounting primitive), with the schema hook (B4): US-009 stores slot identity/kind/hours/re-entry/closure; live occupancy attaches later by `slot_id` in Access / a future capacity-control component — never live counts in Catalog or Inventory claims.

**risk:low → Gate 2 (plan approval) skipped.** Proceeding to Building (write the docs).

<!-- sdlc:stage=ai-review kind=summary -->
**Building complete — codex (gpt-5.5) adversarial review done, all findings folded in.** PR #26.

**Review triage (8 findings, all accepted, fixed in-PR — commit b917c63):**
- [BLOCKING] Capacity-cut floor was `confirmed` — corrected to `confirmed + held` (ADR-010's real invariant is `confirmed + held ≤ capacity`; an in-flight hold already holds headroom).
- [BLOCKING] Multi-entry couldn't live under the table-wide `UNIQUE(ticket_id, event_type)` — now names the concrete mechanism: a **partial unique index** `WHERE event_type='redeemed'` replaces it; `entry`/`exit` get no uniqueness. Single-redemption guarantee is enforced unchanged for the tickets it applies to.
- [SHOULD] Restated the precise Access invariant (single-entry → exactly one `redeemed`, no entry/exit; multi-entry → zero `redeemed`, many entry/exit).
- [SHOULD] Case 2 wording `occupancy` → `confirmed+held demand` (occupancy is the out-of-scope primitive).
- [SHOULD] Reconciled spike vs ADR-005: the cut *behaviour* is decided here; only its *storage representation* is deferred to the inventory ticket.
- [SHOULD] Added the closure/archive cross-rule (archive stays legal regardless of `closure.status`; closure never becomes a 4th lifecycle value).
- [NIT ×2] ADR-013 confirmed-vs-held expiry phrasing; §Verdict anchor link.

No blocking findings survive; no incidental backlog tickets spun off (all were doc-precision fixes to the decision itself). One codex pass only, per protocol. Cross-links verified.

**→ needs:human (Gate 3).** Review-guide posted on PR #26. Spike is docs-only — no CI/`make check` surface. Stopping; no further pushes.

objective.note: De-risk the load-bearing ADR-005 slot abstraction before US-009 hardens the schema: prove one dated-slot model survives re-entry, mid-day capacity change, and weather closure, or record a scoped exception.

scope.note: IN: written analysis + ADR-005 amendment modelling the three stress cases against a candidate slot shape; the catalog-slot-vs-inventory-claim attribute boundary per case; the concrete attribute set + state machine US-009 implements; a PASS/exception verdict. OUT: any production code, migration, or endpoint (spike); the actual claim-path mechanics for shared capacity (deferred to TKT-4/TKT-14).

uncertainties.note: This spike IS the epic's central uncertainty; its output resolves it. No pending product decision beyond the owner ratifying the resulting ADR amendment at review.

dependencies.note: No open blockers. Blocks US-009 (TKT-51) — that story cannot start its schema until this verdict lands.

approach.note: Analysis grounded in the M1 catalog baseline (performances = single-redemption slot) and the ADR-005 §Consequences pressure list; produce the attribute/state-machine shape as an ADR-005 amendment (or a new ADR if a scoped exception is needed). Timeboxed, read-only.

first_slice.note: The deliverable is the decision doc itself — reviewable and demoable as the written verdict + attribute shape.

success.note: COS = the 3 ACs; exit is the recorded verdict (unified model holds with a documented attribute shape, or a scoped-exception ADR), leaving US-009 with a decided schema. No make check surface (docs only).
